definition: Producing fluent natural language text from a model, whether from a prompt, structured data, or other context.
details: Producing fluent natural language text from a model, whether from a prompt, structured data, or other context. It is the core capability of language models and is evaluated with metrics such as perplexity, BLEU, and human preference judgments.

explainer.lead: Text generation produces fluent natural language text from a model, given a prompt, structured data, or other context. It matters because it is the core capability of language models.

tiers.eli5: It is a model writing sentences one after another, like autocomplete that keeps going and produces whole paragraphs.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers prompt models to generate text and evaluate output with perplexity, BLEU, and human preference judgments. The pitfall is trusting a single automatic metric when human preference is what matters for fluency and usefulness.
tiers.paperLevel: Producing fluent natural language text from a model, whether from a prompt, structured data, or other context; evaluated with metrics such as perplexity, BLEU, and human preference judgments.

explainer.example: Given a short prompt, a language model continues writing a full paragraph of fluent prose.
